claims.statement: The Commission's PVGIS provides API-accessible estimates of monthly and yearly PV production using weather and system parameters, while EU rules support access to metering data.
Demand hypothesis: financiers and ESCOs will pay for neutral settlement because energy performance contracts tie payment to contractually guaranteed measured savings.

contrary_evidence: Monitoring portals already show energy production and faults.
Small solar contracts may not include formal performance guarantees.

economics.acquisition_route: Pilot through the family solar business, then sell portfolios through lenders and installer groups.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 150 MW monitored at 2 PLN per kWp monthly can create 3.6 million PLN recurring revenue plus settlements and founder equity above 5 million PLN in five years.
economics.founder_time: Three to four hours daily for models and channel onboarding.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 85-92% margin after automated data normalization.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 3 MW monitored at 2 PLN per kWp monthly repays initial capital within eighteen months.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 1-3 PLN per kWp monthly plus 3-8% of settled credits.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Each financed system needs monthly monitoring and annual true-up for its contract life.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A growing portfolio of normalized system performance and settlement outcomes improves baselines and underwriting.
fingerprint.customer: Commercial solar installers, ESCOs, lessors, lenders, and property owners.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Solar finance providers and installer networks embed it in performance-guaranteed contracts.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: The API freezes baselines, normalizes meter and inverter data, and issues an auditable credit or no-credit statement.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The installer, lessor, or financier pays per kWp monitored and per annual settlement.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A monthly or annual guarantee misses target and parties dispute weather, load, downtime, curtailment, or tariff adjustments.

founder_fit: The family solar company offers immediate data and contracting context.
Quantitative baselining closely matches the founder's data-science skills.
risks: Baseline disputes can become contractual or legal disputes.
Missing meter data can make settlements inconclusive.

structure.control_point: The versioned baseline and accepted adjustment ledger.
structure.critical_dependency: Meter and inverter access plus standardized guarantee clauses.

thesis: A neutral measurement engine can reconcile promised solar savings against weather, meter, inverter, tariff, and outage evidence for financed commercial systems.
title: Solar Performance Guarantee Settlement Engine
uncertainties: The share of Polish commercial systems with guarantees is unknown.
Financier willingness to accept a third-party method is unverified.
